items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] So Freddie Green was doing his thing back then. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, in Renaissance Italy when Monteverdi did “Orfeo” he had his Freddie Green you know, Federico Verdi.

ctx.x: Well that’s exactly it. And because the guitar covers so many different stylistic areas. I mean you play clarinet, sure you can be playing Dixieland or you could be playing Klezmer or playing with an orchestra or doubling on saxophone and doing studio work or whatever. But you’re not going to be playing bluegrass for example. And maybe playing like Greek folk music or something, but in certain musical contexts it doesn’t fit. But the guitar kind of fits everywhere. And sometimes even when it fits it gets ignored.…
So Freddie Green was doing his thing back then.
Yeah, in Renaissance Italy when Monteverdi did “Orfeo” he had his Freddie Green you know, Federico Verdi.
